hypothesis: With the number dev's --auto-tier planner writes, a 1628-token prompt has the CUDA chain's routed-expert buffers refused on an L4 and the host computes them from there on; without the number the prompt reads on the card, so its first token comes sooner (prompt tok/s = prompt tokens / TTFT).
command: cd c && make qwen38 CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_89 && env COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPU=0 COLI_VULKAN=0 COLI_TEMP=0 USAGE_SAVE=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=6 SNAP=<model> [CUDA_EXPERT_GB=21.660] N_NEW=64 COLI_USAGE=<history.usage> ./qwen38 128 8 <prompt>

hardware.cpu: a Colab L4 VM: 12 threads (nproc), 6 physical cores (the plan's OMP_NUM_THREADS), Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.20GHz (lscpu) + NVIDIA L4 (23034 MiB, 22564 MiB free, sm_89)
hardware.ram: 53.0 GiB, no swap; the GGUF (74 GiB) does not fit it
hardware.storage: the VM's disk (overlay, 194GB free); the file cache evicted before each run

quality.method: each side generates the same 64 tokens (greedy: COLI_TEMP=0) in all its runs (long-prompt.txt's summary), so each speed is of one computation; the two sides' texts have the same first 16 words and then differ: with A the prompt's routed experts ran on the host, with B on the card, and the two sum in a different order (not isolated), so the texts are not compared further
